title: Designing Your Life: How to Build a Well-Lived, Joyful Life
author: Bill Burnett
Dave Evans
target_audience: Adults at career or life crossroads
Recent college graduates planning their futures
Anyone hoping to approach life and work with creativity
Readers interested in applying design thinking to personal challenges
core_themes: Applying design thinking to personal and professional life
Reframing failures as opportunities for learning
Building a life aligned with your values and interests
Iterative problem-solving for life’s big questions
primary_purpose: To empower individuals to approach their careers and lives as designers would: using curiosity, creativity, and iterative prototyping to create a meaningful and fulfilling life that reflects their values.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, encouraging, and practical—with anecdotes and real stories
structure_format.organization: Structured around design thinking concepts and practical exercises, with each chapter focusing on a stage or tool of the process (e.g., empathy, ideation, prototyping)
features: Real-world case studies of life design
Graphical models and frameworks (e.g., Odyssey Plans, Good Time Journal)

key_concepts_lessons: Life is not a single problem to be solved, but a design challenge to be explored.
Design thinking—typically used in product and innovation fields—can be applied to life planning.
Curiosity, bias to action, reframing, and radical collaboration are essential mindsets.
Prototyping experiences (e.g., interviews, trying new roles) reduces risk and leads to innovation in life choices.
There are many possible ‘good’ lives, not just one path; Odyssey Planning helps envision different futures.
Work and life satisfaction come from aligning what you do with what you believe and enjoy.
Failures and roadblocks are inevitable, but can be re-framed as wayfinding clues.
notable_features: Adaptation of Stanford University’s popular life design course
Brings design thinking into everyday life decision-making
Includes practical tools like mind maps and Odyssey Plans
Inclusive and supportive approach to navigating uncertainty
cultural_historical_context: Emerging from the 21st-century quest for purposeful work and holistic life design, the book captures growing use of design thinking beyond technology—responding to increasing complexity in modern career and lifestyle trajectories.
reception_impact: Widely adopted in universities, career counseling, and coaching
Praised for innovative and practical approach
Inspired workshops, workbooks, and a sequel ('Designing Your Work Life')
Some critics find exercises more helpful with group/facilitated support
comparable_titles: What Color Is Your Parachute? by Richard N. Bolles
The Art of Possibility by Rosamund Stone Zander and Benjamin Zander
Range: Why Generalists Triumph in a Specialized World by David Epstein
